provenance.method: Practical discovery question assembled from reviewed ND Oracle Concepts and claimless Resource listings. The route distinguishes descriptive information, jurisdiction and access from claims that a strategy or service will work for an individual.

question: Where can I learn about AAC or communication that does not depend on speech?
why_it_matters: People who cannot reliably use speech need routes that do not treat spoken language as the only valid form of communication.
current_understanding: Communication Matters is the current UK specialist route in the catalogue for learning what AAC is and how assessment/provision can work. Cboard is one open-source communication-board option to inspect, and mainstream devices also include typed-to-speech and visual communication features. AAC selection is individual: access method, vocabulary, motor control, language, partner support and the person's own preferences matter, so ND Oracle does not nominate one system as best.
evidence_needed: Independent comparative evidence across AAC systems and access methods.
More governed lived-experience routes from AAC users with different communication and motor profiles.
reopening_conditions: UK AAC provision or funding routes change.
New reviewed AAC systems or AAC-user perspectives are added.
dissent: High-tech AAC is not the only valid communication method; unaided communication, signs, gestures, writing and low-tech systems can also be central.
